Subject: Reserved pool — elevated p95 and 429s since 03:00 UTC

Hi Mina,

We're seeing a sustained degradation for our production endpoints that are on Redwood Dedicated (reserved pool). Metrics since ~03:00 UTC: p50 ~140ms (baseline 100ms), p95 jumped from ~120ms to ~1.8s, and about 4.7% of requests returned 429s in the last hour. Error-rate correlates with longer prompts, but the traffic volume hasn't increased on our side.

We have an SLA that guarantees reserved throughput and predictable latency; this behavior is causing user-visible failures for transaction enrichment (many retries). Can you please confirm whether this is a capacity or routing issue on Redwood? We've attached a short CSV with sample timestamps and request IDs.

Attachments: [latency-samples.csv (text/csv)]

We need an urgent bridge and an ETA for mitigation. If you want logs or temporary key access, we can provide.

Thanks,

Hi all — quick engineering readout from the bridge (attached: pool-utilization.png).

What we observe:
- Dedicated pool for LedgerBank is saturated on 6/8 workers. GPU utilization per-worker is high (avg 92%) with frequent long-tail GC/VM stalls due to large KV cache blowouts for a subset of requests.
- Token distribution shows a small fraction (~3.8%) of sessions producing very long sequences ( > 10k tokens cumulative) causing batch size variance and KV churn.
- Autoscale did not add burst nodes because the pool was configured with strict reserved capacity and burst/autoscale was constrained by a bug in the policy evaluation for "burst_allowed: false" on this tenant. We're seeing 429s from internal queueing when worker queues max out.

Immediate mitigations we've applied (03:42–03:55 UTC):
1) Temporarily enabled emergency burst capacity for the pool (added 2 hot nodes).
2) Applied a conservative per-api-key concurrent-token limit for LedgerBank (throttle to reduce KV churn).
3) Rolled a routing rule routing 5% of traffic to quantized-compact variant (lower memory pressure) as a canary.
4) Captured diagnostics bundle and a 1-minute flame trace for the hot workers.

Preliminary impact: p95 dropped from ~1.8s -> ~620ms within 7 minutes after the burst nodes came online; 429 rate down to ~0.6%. Still above target; long-tail sessions remain the dominant signal.

Next steps (owner in parentheses):
- Deep-dive on KV cache eviction pattern and patch policy (marissa).
- Postmortem and configuration fix for burst_policy evaluation bug (infra; priority P0).
- Customer follow-up + proposed credit (mina/evelyn).

Attachments: [pool-utilization.png (image/png), redwood-diagnostics.tar.gz (application/gzip)]

Sarah/Tom — thank you again for raising this and for the bridge time earlier.

Summary of what happened and what we did:
- Root cause (preliminary): reserved pool saturation driven by a subset of long-tail sessions (high cumulative token counts) that caused excessive KV cache churn, combined with a mis-evaluated burst policy that prevented automatic autoscale.
- Immediate actions taken: enabled emergency burst capacity (+2 nodes), applied per-key concurrency limits, and routed a small percentage of traffic to a lower-memory model variant. These changes reduced p95 from ~1.8s to ~600ms and brought 429s down to ~0.6% within ~10 minutes.
- Next steps: Marissa's team will deliver a patch for burst_policy evaluation (P0) and a KV-cache eviction tweak within 48 hours. We'll run a joint capacity tuning session with your SREs next week to tune reserved sizing and token concurrency profiles.

Proposed customer compensation: 2 weeks of service credit on the monthly reserved commitment and a free joint capacity tuning workshop. Evelyn has pre-approved this level; if you prefer a different form of remediation we can discuss. Draft credit doc attached.

We will follow up with a full postmortem and the technical timeline for the patch. Please let me know a good time for the capacity tuning session (we can do Mon/Tue next week).
